methods.label: Work backward using remainders
methods.explanation:
Multiplying by \(7!=5040\) turns the factorial fractions into integers:
\[
3600=2520a_2+840a_3+210a_4+42a_5+7a_6+a_7.
\]
Every term on the right except \(a_7\) is divisible by 7. Since \(a_7\) is an integer with \(0\le a_7<7\), it must be the remainder when 3600 is divided by 7. Thus \(a_7=2\). Subtracting 2 and dividing by 7 gives
\[
514=360a_2+120a_3+30a_4+6a_5+a_6.
\]
Now every term except \(a_6\) is divisible by 6, and \(0\le a_6<6\), so \(a_6\) is the remainder on division by 6. The same structure continues: remove the last coefficient and divide to expose the next one. The successive divisions are
\[
\begin{aligned}
3600&=7\cdot514+2 &&\Rightarrow a_7=2,\\
514&=6\cdot85+4 &&\Rightarrow a_6=4,\\
85&=5\cdot17+0 &&\Rightarrow a_5=0,\\
17&=4\cdot4+1 &&\Rightarrow a_4=1,\\
4&=3\cdot1+1 &&\Rightarrow a_3=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last quotient is \(a_2=1\). Each remainder is uniquely forced by its stated range. The resulting coefficients satisfy all the bounds, and
\[
2520+840+210+0+28+2=3600,
\]
which verifies the original equation after multiplication by \(7!\).

Their sum is \(1+1+1+0+4+2=\boxed9\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

methods.label: Work forward using bounded tails
methods.explanation:
The bounds \(0\le a_i<i\) make each coefficient recoverable from the integer part of a scaled remainder. To justify this, let \(T_k\) be the sum of the terms after \(a_k/k!\), for \(2\le k\le7\). Then
\[
0\le T_k\le\sum_{i=k+1}^{7}\frac{i-1}{i!}.
\]
The identity
\[
\frac{i-1}{i!}=\frac1{(i-1)!}-\frac1{i!}
\]
makes consecutive terms cancel, giving
\[
0\le T_k\le\frac1{k!}-\frac1{7!}<\frac1{k!}.
\]
For \(k=7\), the sum is empty and \(T_7=0\), so the same bound holds.

After earlier terms have been removed, multiplying what remains by \(k!\) therefore gives \(a_k+k!T_k\), with \(0\le k!T_k<1\). Its integer part is exactly \(a_k\).

We can implement this by starting with \(5/7\), multiplying by 2, keeping the integer part, and then multiplying the fractional remainder by 3. Continue with multipliers 4 through 7:
\[
\begin{aligned}
2\cdot\frac57&=1+\frac37 &&\Rightarrow a_2=1,\\
3\cdot\frac37&=1+\frac27 &&\Rightarrow a_3=1,\\
4\cdot\frac27&=1+\frac17 &&\Rightarrow a_4=1,\\
5\cdot\frac17&=0+\frac57 &&\Rightarrow a_5=0,\\
6\cdot\frac57&=4+\frac27 &&\Rightarrow a_6=4,\\
7\cdot\frac27&=2 &&\Rightarrow a_7=2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The tail bound forces every extracted coefficient. All coefficients obey their required ranges, and the final fractional remainder is zero, confirming exact equality. Their sum is \(\boxed9\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
